data.body:
A REAL LLM-Review VOTE HAS BEEN PRODUCED VIA BEDROCK ON THE PRODUCTION GATE, and the pre/post comparison came from an unexpected but better source than the fixture I lost.

THE VOTE (criterion: change id + vote recorded, sidecar provenance provider == 'bedrock').
  Gerrit change 1329 — 'a32a: normalize comment dedup key' — patch set 2, revision d5ec315ae42b.
  rebar-review-bot @ 2026-08-04 00:16:13Z: 'Patch Set 2: LLM-Review+1  [LLM-Review: PASS]  rebar code review passed.'
  Labels now: LLM-Review=+1, Verified=+1.
  code_review artifact 5eb6-38e1-a439-4134, REVIEW_RESULT sidecar:
      provider_provenance.provider              = bedrock
      provider_provenance.model                 = bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
      provider_provenance.capabilities.prompt_cache_style = bedrock
      blocking = 0, advisory = 0
  Note this is ANOTHER SESSION'S change, reviewed by the production bot in the normal course of work — not a change I staged. That is stronger than a synthetic fixture: the gate voted on real traffic.
  The prompt_cache_style flip from 'anthropic' to 'bedrock' is worth calling out separately: it is the capability layer re-deriving from the model PROFILE rather than from a provider-name string, which is the property [rebar:e951-7df6-1851-4d5e]'s provenance record exists to make observable. The pre-cutover baseline I recorded earlier read prompt_cache_style='anthropic' on the same field, so this is a before/after on the capability decision and not only on the provider label.

THE PRE/POST COMPARISON (criterion: the SAME change reviewed pre- and post-cutover, both finding lists recorded). Change 1329 was reviewed on BOTH sides of the cutover:
    PRE  — artifact b8b6-a636-63df-4d58, revision dca5eb7ffd816d6e686a21192861aaf
           provider=anthropic  model=anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6  cache_style=anthropic
           blocking = 1, advisory = 1
    POST — artifact 5eb6-38e1-a439-4134, revision d5ec315ae42bf2e67e12769fdc90cad
           provider=bedrock    model=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6  cache_style=bedrock
           blocking = 0, advisory = 0
  THE HONEST LIMITATION, stated rather than buried: these are the SAME CHANGE but DIFFERENT REVISIONS (patch set 1 vs patch set 2). The author amended between them, so the disappearance of the blocking finding is confounded by a content change and must NOT be read as 'Bedrock is more permissive' or 'Bedrock fixed it'. What the comparison DOES establish is the criterion's actual bar — 'no NEW blocking finding that is an artifact of the provider': the Bedrock review produced ZERO blocking findings, so no new blocking finding appeared. It cannot establish finding-for-finding equivalence, and I am not claiming it does.
  This is weaker than the byte-identical same-revision comparison the criterion envisages. That comparison became unobtainable when 1325 was submitted (a merged change cannot be /rerun — Gerrit answers 409 'change is closed', which per [rebar:c943-1b38-d613-4013] deliberately emits no VOTER_ERROR either). It also sits inside the operator's standing ruling that cross-model verdict comparison is INFORMATIONAL rather than a gate. Four independent pre-cutover Anthropic baselines are on record for contrast (artifacts 1aa5 / fb4f / 76e8 / b8b6), three of them at 0 blocking.

RECOVERY OBSERVED, UNFORCED — the other half of the drill. rebar-gerrit-voter-errors returned OK on its own at 00:19:47Z, about seven minutes after going ALARM at 00:12:47Z, once the probe published a clean interval following the restore. I did not set-alarm-state it back; the alarm recovered because the underlying condition cleared. Together with the forced ALARM->OK transition recorded earlier on the Bedrock alarm, both alarms have now been observed moving in BOTH directions.

AND 34cd'S ALARM FIRED FOR REAL. rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts is in ALARM as of 00:09:45Z, triggered by the genuine AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT {'reason': 'bound-exceeded'} at 00:03:43Z. That alarm existed only in HCL until I applied it earlier today (it was the un-applied drift that had turned main red), and it has now been validated end-to-end by live traffic rather than by inspection. Recorded here because it is evidence for bug 1c39's thesis: the alarm was declared, reviewed, merged and CLOSED while absent from CloudWatch, and would have stayed silent through exactly the event it was built for.
